subject: [PATCH 1/4] virtio_console: copy pipe buffers in splice_write()

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan approved the patch and gave an Acked-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
LGTM.

Acked-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Reviewer Matthew Wilcox pointed out that the memcpy call in the splice_write function is incorrect and should use memcpy_from_page instead to handle page faults correctly.

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch modifies the virtio_console driver to always copy data from pipe buffers when writing to a file using splice_write(). The previous behavior was to try to steal pages from the pipe buffer, but this approach is being removed in preparation for future changes. As a result, the driver now copies the data into its own page before passing it to the host, ensuring that the data remains unchanged. This change affects the virtio_console.c file and is part of a larger series of patches.

reviews.author: Christian Brauner
reviews.summary: The reviewer pointed out that the pipe_to_sg() function in the virtio_console patch has a bug where it does not properly handle compound pages and buffer offsets, leading to incorrect memory accesses and crashes. They provided two examples of this issue and suggested that copying data per page would fix both problems.
reviews.raw_body:
I don't think that works. pipe_to_sg() only clamps len to the
destination page. A pipe buffer however can span multiple pages of a
compound page iircu. And buf->offset can point past the first one.

I found two exmples:

(1) skb_splice_bits() for AF_UNIX and TCP
(2) tracing_buffers_splice_read() with buffer_subbuf_size_kb > 4,

And virtio-trace splices that stuff.

Which means VM_BUG_ON() in memcpy_from_page() fires:

kernel BUG at include/linux/highmem.h:542!
Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
RIP: 0010:pipe_to_sg+0x130/0x150
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 __splice_from_pipe+0x92/0x1e0
 port_fops_splice_write+0x13f/0x1a0
 do_splice+0x3b6/0x8e0
 __do_splice+0x20a/0x230
 __x64_sys_splice+0x97/0x130
 do_syscall_64+0xde/0x4b0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f

Fwiw, the open-coded copy is broken as well. Just on HIGHMEM...

Starting with b46e09667411 ("fuse: enable large folios")
fuse_dev_splice_read() hands out large page cache folios and
kmap_local_page() only maps the first page.

So a fuse server on a 32-bit HIGHMEM guest that splices a WRITE request
into a virtio port crashes mainline:

BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffab000
#PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
#PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
EIP: pipe_to_sg+0x184/0x2b0
Call Trace:
 __splice_from_pipe+0xd6/0x1f0
 port_fops_splice_write+0xf9/0x170
 do_splice+0x2c1/0x810
 __ia32_sys_splice+0x2e7/0x310

So we need to copy per page which would fix both.

reviews.author: Christian Brauner
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the virtio_console code in pipe_to_sg() uses kmap_local_page() to map a single page of a compound page, which can lead to incorrect behavior when copying data from the pipe buffer. They suggested using copy_page_to_iter() instead, as it handles compound pages correctly and is used in similar situations elsewhere in the kernel.

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Linus Torvalds pointed out that the patch introduces unnecessary complexity by making a single memcpy() into a more complex operation, and suggested removing it since HIGHMEM is dead and will be removed anyway.

Reviewer expressed frustration and skepticism towards the patch, questioning its necessity due to lack of reported issues.
reviews.raw_body:
This boils down to one memcpy.

HIGHMEM is dead. Nobody sane uses it. It *will* go away. It's already
effectively never ever used.

There are some broken 32-bit arm setups that use it, and legacy museum
32-bit x86.

Don't make one memcpy() that can be inlined become this garbage:

---

just because of broken shit that nobody has ever complained about or ever hit.

              Linus

reviews.author: Christian Brauner
reviews.summary: Reviewer Christian Brauner expressed strong disagreement (CONTENTIOUS) with the patch, stating that if the decision is to ignore HIGHMEM bugs, then the try_steal() function should be completely removed for v7.5.
reviews.raw_body:
If that's the official new stance than I'm very happy.

I went by what we have historically done and very recent history still
has us fixing HIGHMEM shit.

So if this is an official thing that we can now say: "Fuck it, we don't
care about HIGHMEM and will ignore bugs because". Then why can't we just
completely kill it for say v7.5?

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that HIGHMEM is legacy and will be removed in the future, suggesting that new bugs introduced by this patch should not be a concern.
reviews.raw_body:
I definitely want to remove HIGHMEM entirely in the not too distant
future. And before we remove it, we can most definitely document the
fact that we will not be worried about insane users.

And things like security issues count as "insane user": if you use
HIGHMEM outside of controlled embedded setups or museum pieces you get
to keep both pieces when it breaks.

IOW, it's legacy. We should aim to not introduce *new* bugs to it, but
if there are pre-existing bugs they very much count as "don't care",
this will be removed soon.

I think the only reason it wasn't removed a couple of years ago
already is basically a few old 32-bit ARM platforms that still used
it.

Those platforms still exist, and I predict that they'll still exist
next year, but if those users have to stay at the current LTS kernel,
that's fine.

                  Linus

reviews.author: Arnd Bergmann
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested adding Kconfig dependencies to mark highmem-related issues as broken when known buggy or intentionally breaking functionality for non-users

Arnd Bergmann noted two problems he encountered while attempting to convert GFP_HIGHMEM allocations to use lowmem: movable allocations imply highmem, and internal tmpfs users may not want highmem or movable pages but are currently defaulting to GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed. There is also the option of adding Kconfig dependencies to
mark things that are known broken with highmem when we either know
that it is buggy, or we have a good reason to break something that
none of those remaining users should be using.

---

I tried to push for what I thought was an aggressive timeline
last year, but that would still keep the Arm bits for a couple more
LTS releases and only gradually reduce the scope of highmem in the
meantime, removing support from architectures, file systems, and
drivers where possible. See https://lwn.net/Articles/1051010/
for a summary of my talk in Tokyo, including the slides and
a link to the video for anyone wanting more details.

I also prepared a number of patches towards this, but have so
far not been great at following up to get them merged, sorry
about that.
I definitely still want to revisit this soon, in particular the
bits about defaulting to VMSPLIT_2G_OPT, and probably my patch
to allow having (limited) discontiguous lowmem on Arm systems
with a large MMIO hole.

Scope-wise I think we absolutely need zsmalloc (zram/zswap)
on arm32 to work with GFP_HIGHUSER, but enough people have told me
that they still expect to need anonymous memory and ext4 page
cache for a while, and probably powerpc32. The majority
of __GFP_HIGHMEM allocations can probably just be converted
to use lowmem, which would eliminate a good chunk of kmap()
calls as well. In my attempts to do that, I came across two
problems I'd have to solve though:

 - Movable allocations (GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE) imply highmem.
   while I think only 64-bit architectures support movable
   pages today, we cannot currently express an allocation
   that should be movable on 64-bit but lowmem on 32-bit.

 - Internal users of tmpfs (in particular DRM/GEM) usually
   don't want highmem or movable pages, but actual tmpfs
   does default to GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE. Separating the two
   is complicated.

I added a few people to Cc here that I believe care about
having several more LTS releases with some highmem support
because of existing customer requirements.

     Arnd

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested removing remaining users of legacy 'kmap()' interface to simplify code, potentially eliminating 'pkmap_page_table[]' mess and related constants.
reviews.raw_body:
Lovely.

I'd love to expand on this kind of early removal: anybody want to get
brownie points by just removing the remaining users of the legacy
'kmap()' interface entirely?

I don't think we actually have that many of them. Almost all users
have already been converted to 'kmap_local_page()' and friends.

If we got rid of the legacy kmap() case, I think that would get rid of
the whole "pkmap_page_table[]" mess and the PKMAP_BASE / PKMAP_END /
PKMAP_ADDR games and only use the FIXMAP area.

                   Linus
